clue.text: Acrimony between bloggers (not involving Hitler)?

parts.note: a row between bloggers is a war of posts, a quarrel fought in online messages; and a period that does not involve Hitler is the time after 1945

explanation.surface: A spat between internet writers, carefully noted as having nothing to do with the Nazi leader.
explanation.walkthrough: Split as POST WAR, the answer is a fight between people who post online; read whole, it is the era after the Second World War, when Hitler was no longer involved.
explanation.definitionFit: Two readings: a feud conducted through online posts, and the historical period following the 1939-45 conflict.

clue.text: Mischievous type caught in UKIP's toils — I would leave

indicators.note: caught is placed in the jumbled letters
toils, struggles or entanglements, suggests the party's letters being twisted around
I would leave means the letter I departs from the party's name

parts.note: UKIP is the UK Independence Party
C is the cricket abbreviation for caught

explanation.surface: A troublemaker trapped in the snares of UKIP, from which the speaker would escape.
explanation.walkthrough: Without I, UKIP leaves UKP, rearranged as PUK, and C goes inside. Puck is also a Guardian setter, one of the down themes.
explanation.definitionFit: Puck, Robin Goodfellow in A Midsummer Night's Dream, is the archetypal mischievous sprite.

clue.text: Woman would go to pot here

parts.note: she is the pronoun for a woman
the contraction of would is 'd, as in she'd

explanation.surface: A woman would let herself go downhill in this place.
explanation.walkthrough: 'go to pot' means decline, but here is literal: plants are potted in a potting shed. Shed is also a Guardian setter.
explanation.definitionFit: A garden building where seedlings are potted up is a potting shed.

clue.text: Not having a wash? So a good night

definitions.meaning: a ship's wash is its wake, so this describes a vessel leaving no trail
a night of unbroken sleep, with no waking

explanation.surface: Skipping a bath at bedtime makes for a good night's rest.
explanation.walkthrough: 'wash' looks like bathing; it is the wake behind a boat.
explanation.definitionFit: Without a trail of disturbed water behind it, and also undisturbed sleep, as in deep slumber.

clue.text: King upset American element, having no Latin

indicators.note: upset, in a down clue, means turned upside down so the letters run upwards
having no Latin means the abbreviation for Latin is removed

parts.note: sulfur is the American spelling of the element sulphur

explanation.surface: A monarch overturns an American ingredient because it lacks Latin.
explanation.walkthrough: SULFUR without L is SUFUR, written upwards. William Rufus was William II of England; Rufus is also a Guardian setter.
explanation.definitionFit: William II of England was nicknamed Rufus, for his red face, so he was a king of that name.

clue.text: Place kept in identical taste

indicators.note: the abbreviation for place is held inside the word for identical, as if kept within it

parts.note: identical means same
PL is the standard abbreviation for place, as in street names

explanation.surface: Somewhere that keeps the same flavour every time.
explanation.definitionFit: A taste of something is a small trial portion, the same as a sample offered to try.

clue.text: Charge according to amount employed

parts.note: acc. is the abbreviation for according to
use, as in the use of water, is the amount used or employed

explanation.surface: A fee set by how much is consumed.
explanation.walkthrough: Charge reads like a bill, but it is the verb meaning to blame.
explanation.definitionFit: To charge someone with a crime is to accuse them formally.

clue.text: No artist makes high table in softwood

indicators.note: the high table goes inside the softwood

parts.note: pine is a softwood timber
hi is a short form of high
a list is a table, as in a league table

explanation.surface: A non-painter builds a raised table out of soft timber.
explanation.walkthrough: 'high table' looks like a college dining table; it is HI and LIST. Philistine is also a Guardian setter.
explanation.definitionFit: A philistine is hostile or indifferent to culture and the arts, the opposite of an aesthete.

clue.text: Watch over so many finalists in beauty contest, say

indicators.note: say means the phrase is spoken, giving another phrase with the same sound

parts.words: so many finalists in beauty contest
parts.note: the number eight of belles, beautiful women, as finalists

explanation.surface: A judge keeps watch over the shortlist of a beauty pageant.
explanation.walkthrough: On a ship, eight strokes of the bell mark the end of a four-hour watch. 'Watch over' is a reading of that, not guarding.
explanation.definitionFit: The ship's bell is struck eight times at the end of each watch, signalling that it is over.

clue.text: Mark down dramatist to speak

indicators.note: to speak the dramatist's name means to say it out loud, giving a phrase that sounds the same

parts.note: Anton Chekhov was the Russian dramatist who wrote The Seagull and The Cherry Orchard

explanation.surface: An instruction to downgrade a playwright simply for talking.
explanation.definitionFit: To tick an item off a list is to mark it down as done or recorded.

clue.text: Playing for time, Henry is hurt

indicators.note: Henry stands for time, so one letter is swapped for the other in the word for playing

parts.note: playing a role is acting
H is the symbol for the henry, the unit of inductance

explanation.surface: An actor named Henry, stalling for time on stage, is wounded.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Playing for time' reads as a single idiom, but 'for' is the swap signal: Henry's H replaces the T of time in ACTING.
explanation.definitionFit: Something aching is sore or painful, so hurt as an adjective fits.

clue.text: Endless deception covered by Imogen in this system

parts.note: Imogen is the setter, who refers to herself as me

indicators.note: endless means the word for deception loses its last letter

parts.note: a trick is a deception

explanation.surface: The setter hides a never-ending con within her puzzle system.
explanation.definitionFit: The decimal measuring system based on metres and kilograms is called the metric system.

clue.text: In drink (litres!), Daisy's a hypocrite

indicators.note: the pieces sit in the drink, with the beer measure split around them

parts.note: a pint is a drink of beer
an aster is a daisy-like flower, and the possessive gives the plural-looking ASTERS

explanation.surface: Someone tipsy on litres of drink is exposed: Daisy is a fraud.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In drink' looks like 'drunk', but the beer measure is split open around the other pieces. Daisy looks like a woman's name but is the flower.
explanation.definitionFit: A plaster saint is someone who poses as morally perfect without being so, a sanctimonious pretender.

clue.text: Strange choice firm made for archive medium

indicators.note: strange suggests the letters of choice firm are twisted into an odd new order

explanation.surface: An odd selection a company created for storing records.
explanation.definitionFit: Microfiche, sheets of film holding tiny images of documents, is used for archive storage.

clue.text: His aim, setting crackers?

indicators.note: crackers, meaning mad, signals the letters of aim setting going haywire

explanation.surface: A puzzle-maker's goal: setting crossword clues that are fiendish crackers.
explanation.walkthrough: Nearly an &lit: the whole clue describes a puzzle setter, though 'His' adds nothing to the wordplay. Enigmatist is also a Guardian setter.
explanation.definitionFit: A setter of riddles or puzzles is someone whose aim is to compose crackers, hard brain-teasers.

clue.text: Poison working at this point? It's up in the air

indicators.note: working suggests the letters of poison are being worked into a different shape

parts.note: at this point means here

explanation.surface: Toxin is acting right now, and the situation is unresolved.
explanation.walkthrough: 'It's up in the air' looks like an idiom for uncertainty; here it is literal, a layer of the upper atmosphere.
explanation.definitionFit: This ionised layer lies high in the atmosphere, so it is literally something up in the sky.

clue.text: Birds, sound asleep, hard to rouse

indicators.note: to rouse is to raise or get up, so in a down clue the pieces read upwards

parts.note: snoring is the sound made when asleep
H is the abbreviation for hard, as on pencils

explanation.surface: Birds in a deep slumber that are difficult to wake.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sound asleep' looks like deep sleep; it is the noise a sleeper makes.
explanation.definitionFit: Herons are long-legged wading birds.

clue.text: Draw level shortly

indicators.note: shortly means cut short, so the word for level loses its final letter

parts.note: a tier is a level, as in a tiered cake or stadium

explanation.surface: An instruction to make the score equal soon.
explanation.definitionFit: A drawn match, with equal scores, is a tie in sporting language.

clue.text: Forces new trial in my case and one is held

indicators.note: the jumbled trial goes in the case formed by the word my

parts.note: the word my serves as the case, its two letters enclosing the rest

indicators.note: one is held means the numeral is gripped inside the jumble
new signals that the letters of trial are made into something fresh

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: Armed forces stage a fresh trial in which one person is detained.
explanation.walkthrough: TRIAL rearranged as ILTAR takes I after its L, giving ILITAR between M and Y.
explanation.definitionFit: The armed services collectively are the military, the forces.

clue.text: Constable for one needs good cloth

parts.note: John Constable, the landscape painter, was a Royal Academician, abbreviated RA

explanation.surface: A police officer, for example, requires a decent piece of fabric.
explanation.walkthrough: Constable looks like a policeman but is the painter John Constable.
explanation.definitionFit: A rag is a piece of old cloth used for cleaning.

clue.text: Divided into groups to suppress resistance, not 28

indicators.note: suppressing something holds it down inside, so the letter for resistance goes within

parts.note: factional describes something split into factions or groups
R is the symbol for electrical resistance

explanation.surface: A split body moves to crush opposition, except for one particular member.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is a cross-reference: 28 across means whole, so 'not 28' means partial.
explanation.definitionFit: Fractional means being only a part, the opposite of whole or complete.

clue.text: Girl cuts sister — she uses sharp blades

indicators.note: the girl's name cuts into the abbreviation, splitting it apart

parts.note: Kate is a girl's name

explanation.surface: A girl wounds her sister with a sharp knife.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sharp blades' suggests knives; they are on ice skates.
explanation.definitionFit: An ice skater glides on boots fitted with sharp metal blades.

clue.text: Plain scientist, not one that Shelley imagined

parts.note: plain, meaning outspoken, is frank

indicators.note: not one means the word for one is left out of the scientist's name

parts.note: Albert Einstein, the physicist
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: An ordinary scientist, not the kind Mary Shelley invented.
explanation.walkthrough: Only the first I of EINSTEIN goes.
explanation.definitionFit: Mary Shelley's novel imagined Victor, the scientist who builds a creature, so this name is what she imagined.

clue.text: Vehicle parking for walk

parts.note: a tram is a street vehicle running on rails
P is the road-sign abbreviation for parking

explanation.surface: A car park to be used for a stroll.
explanation.walkthrough: Tramp is also a Guardian setter.
explanation.definitionFit: To tramp is to walk heavily or a long way, a trek on foot.

clue.text: Rich cloak announced for 1 of 6 church leaders

indicators.note: announced means spoken out, so a word with the same sound is entered

parts.note: a pall is a rich cloth or cloak, as draped over a coffin

explanation.surface: A splendid cloak is proclaimed for one of six bishops.
explanation.walkthrough: Six popes took this name. Paul is also a Guardian setter.
explanation.definitionFit: Six popes have taken this name, so it names one of six leaders of the Roman Catholic church.

clue.text: Socratic method so revolutionary for 1 of 8 here

parts.note: Socrates taught by question and answer, Q and A

indicators.note: revolutionary means turning round, so the little word so is reversed

explanation.surface: Socrates' questioning approach is so radical for one of the people here.
explanation.walkthrough: The down answers hide eight Guardian setters' pseudonyms; this one is among them, and like ENIGMATIST it is defined only as a setter.
explanation.definitionFit: Qaos is a Guardian crossword setter, one of the eight setters' names among the down entries of this puzzle.

clue.text: Perhaps boxer's vulnerable point finally hit at the end — it could be curtains

parts.note: a boxer's chin is the weak spot, as a punch there causes a knockout

indicators.note: finally picks out the closing letter of hit

parts.note: Z is the end of the alphabet

explanation.surface: A boxer struck on the chin at the end of the bout: it could be curtains for him.
explanation.walkthrough: 'it could be curtains' looks like the fighter's doom; literally it is a fabric curtains are made of.
explanation.definitionFit: Chintz is a glazed printed cotton commonly made into curtains and upholstery.

clue.text: In front of a parent, shake chain

indicators.note: the word for shake goes in front of the rest in the answer

parts.note: a dog's tail wags, a wag being a shake
mama is a word for mother, a parent

explanation.surface: Someone in front of their mother rattles a chain.
explanation.walkthrough: Chain looks like a metal chain; it is a restaurant chain.
explanation.definitionFit: Wagamama is a British chain of Japanese-style noodle restaurants.

clue.text: Not 20 conservationists in the country

indicators.note: the conservationists are placed in the country's name

parts.note: Eire is the Irish name for Ireland
NT is the National Trust, the British heritage conservation charity

explanation.surface: Environmentalists living out in the countryside.
explanation.walkthrough: 20 across means partial, so 'Not 20' means whole.
explanation.definitionFit: Something not partial is whole or complete, with no part missing.

clue.text: Girl is stupid to return to pub

parts.note: PH is the abbreviation for public house, a pub

indicators.note: to return means to go back, so the word for stupid is read backwards

parts.note: silly means stupid

explanation.surface: A young woman is foolish to go back to the bar.
explanation.definitionFit: Phyllis is a woman's first name, from the Greek for leafy.
